correctness.rationale: The distance to each face is derived from global dominance among all simple developed cube-face paths. An exact-rational full path enumeration verifies 28 top-to-bottom and 26 top-to-fixed-side paths; affine squared-distance comparisons at four corners cover continuous squares. Canonical paths cross their advertised faces, so candidates are attainable. The circle-square, rectangle and triangular wedge integrals reproduce every CDF branch, an exact rational monomial calculation checks moments through order eight, and the opposite-face sector Taylor expansion proves both tail coefficients. Finite randomized sampling is only corroborative. Singular edge/vertex boundaries follow by continuity.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison attributes the source/target cube unfolding and centroid three-face geometry to Goldstone–Roca–Suzzi Valli (2020), and restricts new content to the evaluated intrinsic geodesic-length CDF over all six faces, exact even-moment sequence and two-term farthest tail. Earlier literature on vertex geodesics, cut loci, geodesic flow and Euclidean random distances does not contain an equivalent evaluated statement in the inspected material. Research-record searches on matching objects/quantities returned no identical law. Residual historical and access risks are stated; negative search is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The pushforward of normalized cube surface area under intrinsic distance from a natural face-center basepoint is a canonical metric-measure invariant. Its complete elementary CDF, rational even-moment hierarchy and sharp two-term farthest-point tail supply reproducible quantitative benchmarks. Integrating circular segments across top, side and opposite-face Voronoi changes is a mathematically motivated calculation beyond listing known shortest path images. It does not claim broad arbitrary-source classification.
